scenes.text: This week you can watch pieces of Halley's Comet burn up in the sky.
It's called the Orionid meteor shower, and it peaks around October twenty first and twenty second.
Every year, Earth flies through the dusty trail Halley's Comet leaves behind.
That dust hits our air at about sixty six kilometers per second, and glows as it burns up.
Look up before dawn, and you might see fifteen to twenty per hour.
The comet itself won't come back until twenty sixty one.
Will you go outside and look tonight?

title: You can see Halley's Comet this week (sort of) ☄️
caption: The Orionid meteor shower peaks around Oct 21-22. Those shooting stars are dust from Halley's Comet hitting our atmosphere at about 66 km per second. The comet itself returns in 2061!
